root_idea.summary: The root has two principal semantic axes: turning aside or inclining, and the shell of a mollusk.
root_idea.development: The notion of turning aside extends to bodily deviation, animals that wait or refuse to approach, and the side of a mountain; the shell sense forms a separate lexical branch with related anatomical and maritime extensions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the supported singular citation form صَدَفٌ; the Quranic occurrence is its inflected dual.

senses.definition: To turn sharply away from; to shun or avoid.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic construction, it is used with عَنْ and denotes emphatic turning away from or rejection of something, especially divine signs. The verb may be understood as turning aside, back, or away.

senses.definition: The two facing sides or cliffs of a mountain or mountain pass.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the definite dual الصَّدَفَيْنِ, referring to two mountain sides or cliffs meeting or facing one another, with a passage or valley between them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An outward turning or twisting of a hoof, pastern, or foreleg; a conformational deviation in a horse or camel.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Descriptions include close-set thighs with outward-set hoofs, crooked forelegs, or an outward inclination of the foot; the precise description varies by animal and authority.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To find, meet, encounter, or come upon someone or something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It can also take an affair as an object and a complement describing that affair as suitable or in accord with one's wish.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Being opposite, facing, or matching one another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional verbal-noun use describing two things as mutually aligned or facing each other.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn someone or something away, turn it back, or cause it to revert.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb may be transitive or intransitive; the transitive use takes the person or thing caused to turn away as its object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To present oneself or take an oblique course, moving alternately to the right and left.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Attested especially of a camel or camels moving among high places or along ascents; the usage is equated with تَعَرَّضَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of two mountain sides: to meet and face each other.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used reciprocally of opposing sides of a mountain or similar terrain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Anything high or lofty, such as a wall, mountain, or other substantial structure.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun can denote a lofty natural or constructed object; this is distinct from its use for a mountain side or shell.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A shell or shell-valve of a mollusk, especially the covering of a pearl; by extension, an oyster or other shellfish.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is also used collectively or individually for the shell-bearing creature and has the plural أَصْدَافٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The concha, or broad external cavity, of the ear.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized anatomical extension of the shell sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pair of anatomical sockets or hollows in which the heads of bones are set.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is applied to the hip sockets and, in some usage, to corresponding sockets of the scapula.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece of flesh resembling cartilage that grows in a head wound next to the skull.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare figurative or specialized anatomical usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Waves of the sea.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded as a plural lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of predatory animal; according to another view, a bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The identification is reported with lexical variation between a beast of prey and a bird.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel of a particular, excellent sort.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The adjective is also explained as a tribal nisba, connected with the Ṣadaf group or a sub-tribe of Kinda.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Testaceous; pertaining to shells or shell-bearing creatures.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A relational adjective derived from the shell sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who turns the face away or avoids affectionate kisses.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a woman who turns away from her husband or does not desire kisses, and also to a man who turns his face whenever addressed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person with foul-smelling breath or mouth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to either a female or a male according to the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A she-camel that will not approach the watering place until it is left unoccupied.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized description of an animal's refusal or delay in approaching the watering trough.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Camels that wait behind other camels at a watering trough until the drinkers have gone away.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A plural form describing animals that defer entering the watering place until it is free.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person often afflicted by diseases.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Recorded as a colloquial or vulgar usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Veiled, concealed, covered, or protected.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive participial description equivalent to being screened or kept from view.

cautions: The Quranic nominal occurrence is an inflected definite dual, الصَّدَفَيْنِ; it is displayed under the supported singular citation form صَدَفٌ.

Classical authorities record variant vocalizations and interpretations for the Quranic dual; the public sense follows the secure QAC occurrence and the mountain-side interpretation supported in the lexical evidence.
